title: Lab - Create filesystems and mount them at boot
description: Format, mount, and make it permanent.
scenario: Format, mount, and make it permanent. This lab is a skeleton: the tasks name what to do and how to check it; work them on your own VM and expand your notes as you go.
environment_setup:
# Any Linux VM with sudo will do - Ubuntu 22.04 or Rocky 9, 2 vCPU, 2 GB RAM.
# Snapshot it before you start so a broken task is a revert away.
sudo -i
hostnamectl
cleanup: # Revert the VM snapshot, or undo the changes you made by hand.

tasks.title: Task 1 - Format
tasks.instructions: Create an xfs filesystem labelled data on /dev/sdc1.

tasks.title: Task 2 - Mount
tasks.instructions: Mount it at /data and add a UUID-based fstab entry.
tasks.solution:
mkdir -p /data && mount /dev/sdc1 /data
echo "UUID=$(blkid -s UUID -o value /dev/sdc1) /data xfs defaults 0 0" >> /etc/fstab

tasks.title: Task 3 - Grow
tasks.instructions: Extend the filesystem after the partition was enlarged.
